full_judgment: 7. Mr. Aminul Huq, the learned Attorney- General, on the other hand, argues that the Special Judge took into consideration the police record and the material seized by the police and after hearing the petitioner under section 241A CrPC framed the charge and as such it can not be said that the Special Judge had no material for framing the charge and the proceeding pending before him is liable to be quashed. He submitted that the police record includes First Information Report, the statement recorded under section 161 CrPC, the Case Diary and the papers, documents, instruments seized by the police. He argues that the Special Judge has examined the aforementioned papers and examined the accused under section 241A CrPC and formed the opinion that there is ground for presuming that the petitioner has committed the offence charged with and framed the charge under section 242 CrPC. Therefore, according to the Attorney-General provision of section 241A CrPC having had been complied with by the Special Judge, the charge framed cannot be said to be without any ingredient for the offence. He says that when before the Special Judge there was material to form the opinion that there is ground for presumption of commission of offence by the accused the proceeding before him can not be whittled merely on the ground that the charges as framed under section 242 CrPC do not disclose any ingredient of offence and the proceeding is abuse of the process of court. Secondly, he submitted that assuming that the advice rendered under Clause (2) of Article 58 of the Constitution does not empower a court to enquire into the advice rendered by the petitioner to the President but the court is not disentitled to enquire into the basis upon which the advice was rendered. The learned Counsel for the petitioner and the learned Attorney-General cited a large number of decisions in support of their respective contentions but I shall refer these which I consider relevant in my judgment as I proceed to pronounce the Judgment
